events.title: Flash Flood near Atlas
events.description: 2 deaths. Upshur County. Stonecoal Lake Road began to flood and stranded a vehicle. At 630 PM EST, two people drowned after their vehicle was swept away by flash flooding from the Right Fork of Stonecoal Creek while traveling along County Route 7. Time is an estimate provided by law enforcement. Around 7 PM EST, floodwaters also trapped a person on top of a camper along Stonecoal Lake Road.

events.title: Flash Flood near Roneys Pt
events.description: 9 deaths. Ohio County. Reports of flash flooding began to come in around 8:30pm, starting near Peters Run Road and Battle Run Road. The water quickly rose along Little Wheeling Creek and the tributaries into Little Wheeling Creek. Emergency management reported at 9pm that there were several water rescues involving stranded vehicles and water rescues from buildings, especially along Route 40/National Road from Elm Grove to the PA State line.

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Aldridge
events.description: 1 death. Jefferson County. A tree blew down onto an occupied golf cart at Locust Hill Golf Course, killing one occupant and critically injuring another.

events.title: Flash Flood near Keystone
events.description: 3 deaths. Mcdowell County. Major flash flooding occurred in and around Welch. Homes and businesses were surrounded by water, roads and underpasses became impassable, and cars were stranded. People became trapped in their vehicles on Riverside Drive before the Havaco bridge. In Kimball, water entered multiple homes, businesses, and cars. A vehicle with five occupants drove into floodwaters and was swept into the Tug Fork River. Two people were able to make it to safety while the other three occupants perished.

events.title: Flood near Cedar Grove
events.description: 1 death. Wood County. A man drove past high water signs on Nicolette Road. The vehicle became stranded in flood waters and submerged, claiming the life of the occupant.

events.title: Flood near Cedar Grove
events.description: 1 death. Wood County. In Davisville, a vehicle drove into flood water occurring within a large dip in the road along Nicolette Road, overturned and submerged. The single occupant was unable to egress.

events.title: Flood near Spencer
events.description: 1 death. Roane County. Tanner Run flooded the Spencer Middle School baseball field. A fatality occurred when a man fell asleep in the dugout and was swept away. Local responders found him later that afternoon after the flood waters had receded.

events.title: Flood near Long Branch
events.description: 1 death. Fayette County. Continuous rounds of rain led to prolonged flooding around the Pax area. High water was first observed on the evening of February 16th along Packs Branch Road and portions of Paint Creek Road. The next morning, Paint Creek remained out of its banks and continued to spill onto Paint Creek Road. A vehicle drove into the flooded road and was swept away along with an infant. Local authorities later found the infant had drowned.

events.title: Flash Flood near Kodol
events.description: 1 death. Wetzel County. Secondary roads in the vicinity of Wileyville and Jacksonburg have been closed due to flooding. At around 10:30 AM, one 20 year old woman was killed when she was swept off of a bridge in Wileyville by flood waters.

events.title: Flash Flood near West Huntington
events.description: 1 death. Cabell County. Significant flash flooding occurred in Cabell County. The hardest hit area was the Enslow Park area where over 100 homes and many vehicles were inundated as Fourpole Creek flooded. Some vehicles were swept away. Route 10 was closed due to flash flooding near Huntinton High School, Route 60 was impassable at the East Mall Road intersection in Barboursville, and flood waters entered Davis Creek Elementary School. A 63 year old man drowned in flood waters along Kilgore Creek Road in Milton. The man was working on a farm tractor and high water swept him away.

events.title: Flood near Cisco
events.description: 1 death. Ritchie County. The body of an elderly man was found after being swept away by floodwaters due to Hughes River being out of its banks. The vehicle was spotted by passing motorists near State Route 47 in the Cisco area nearly submerged underwater.

events.title: Hail near Petersburg
events.description: 1 death (indirect). Grant County. Golf ball size hail was reported at Petersburg High School. Slippery, hail-covered roads caused a traffic crash that resulted in a fatality in the 2000 block of WV-55 North Fork Highway.

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Wellington
events.description: 1 death. Roane County. A 55 year old female was killed when a large oak tree fell on her while she was getting her mail.

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Redhill
events.description: 1 death. Preston County. One man was killed and two were injured when a tree fell on them while on a kayaking trip near Seven Islands on the Cheat River. Story reported here: https://www.wvnews.com/prestoncountynews/news/kayaker-who-died-on-cheat-river-identified/article_23cdb16e-5aeb-5a46-90b5-6eedca78115c.html.

events.title: Flood near Marrtown
events.description: 2 deaths. Wood County. Numerous roads were flooded across northern Wood County. Worthington Creek came out of its banks east of Parkersburg closing the intersection of Core Road and 36th Street. Old St. Marys Pike was also closed due to flooding on Worthington Creek. Water from Carpenter Run closed portions of Waverly Road near Waverly. ||About 6 miles northeast of Parkersburg, a vehicle became stranded on Laurel Creek Road while trying to drive through high water from Laurel Creek. The SUV was washed into the creek before first responders arrived. There were two people in the vehicle, a father and daughter.…

events.description: 1 death. Wood County. Remove.

events.title: Heavy Rain near Mattie
events.description: 1 death. Roane County. A toddler was left unattended, playing along Green Creek in southern Roane County, near the community of Walton. It was believed that the young girl was swept away by the swollen creek. Rescuers found the girl a short distance downstream but were not able to resuscitate her.

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Fairview
events.description: 1 death (indirect). Mason County. A West Virginia DOH worker was killed during the cleanup of one tree down on Union Campground Road. The worker was removing the tree from the road when it rolled over onto him.

events.title: Flash Flood near Hodges
events.description: 1 death. Cabell County. Water rose rapidly on several local streams and creeks resulting in roadway blockages and homes surrounded. The hardest hit area was along Green Valley Road where 50 homes sustained damage from high water. The public witnessed a car drive rapidly into flooded waters along Green Valley Road. After assisting the driver and one passenger out of the vehicle, they called 911. Rescuers were unable to get the second passenger out, before the vehicle floated away. A 56 year old woman drowned in the vehicle.||Additional flooding occurred along Fourpole creek in Huntington from runoff to the south.…

events.title: Flash Flood near Rainelle
events.description: 16 deaths. Greenbrier County. Unprecedented flash flooding occurred across large parts of Greenbrier County but especially in a swath across the central part of the county where an estimated 6 to 10 inches of rain fell in less than 12 hours. The first flood-related report was received at 100 PM EDT (1200 PM EST) as a portion of Highway 20 in western Greenbrier County became impassable south of Quinwood due to a mudslide and debris in the road. By 130 PM (1230 EST) there were several reports of flash flooding in the community of Rupert which required the evacuation of a nursing home and a vehicle rescue. Portions of Route…

events.title: Flood near King
events.description: 4 deaths. Kanawha County. The flood of record occurred on the lower Elk River around Clendenin. ||Two women died. They were trying to save family heirlooms in the basement of a home in Elkview. In likely their last cell phone contact, 1 of the 2 women described the scene, as like the Titanic. An elderly man also died in his home in Elkview. Another young woman died, but the situation was unknown. | |Both the flash flooding and the river flooding were severe, but the amount of damage from the record river flooding was likely higher in Kanawha County, than the damage from the flash flooding.

events.title: Flash Flood near Millwood
events.description: 1 death. Jackson County. Flash flooding occurred in scattered locations, mostly in the northern half of the county. In Ravenswood, a small stream along Utah Road called Lick Run is usually ankle deep. It rose 6 feet. A 4 year old toddler slipped into the water. The grandfather jumped in, but could not rescue him. His body was found the following day, about a quarter mile away. ||A preliminary damage assessment was done in this county. It had 10 homes destroyed and about 2 dozen with damage.

events.title: Flood near Island Branch
events.description: 2 deaths. Kanawha County. Severe flash flooding occurred in the northeastern portion of the county. Streams such as Jordan Creek, Doctors Creek, Thorofare Run, Little Sandy Creek, Wills Creek, and the lower reaches of Big Sandy Creek caused much destruction. ||Little Sandy Creek inundated one large culvert over the only road access to a shopping plaza. The road collapsed. Many shoppers were stranded. About 200 people slept in their vehicles overnight, before walking out on the 24th. ||A 62 year old male drowned along Jordan Creek. He did not leave his home. His small house was washed away. A 47 year old female drowned…

events.title: Heavy Rain near Harts
events.description: 1 death. Lincoln County. During the night, a car with 4 occupants attempted to drive through a natural stream crossing off of Route 19 near Harts. A few mobile homes were located on the opposite side. The stream was Big Harts Creek. The stream was swollen, but still well within its bank. No flooding was occurring.||The car got stuck in the stream bed. Everyone made it to safety. State Police said 2 individuals went back to the car to get some items out. Both were swept away by the water. One was rescued. The body of a 48 year old female was found after dawn, about a mile down stream.

events.title: Lightning near Gatewood
events.description: 1 death. Fayette County. Lightning struck a tree near where 3 teenage boys were fishing on a small residential pond. The location is off of Elverton Road and near the Bridge Haven Golf Course. ||One boy died, the 2 others were injured.

events.title: Flash Flood near Cove Gap
events.description: 1 death. Wayne County. Numerous streams overflowed and blocked roads. Examples were Newcomb Creek and Lynn Creek near East Lynn, Lick and Cove Creeks near Kiahsville, plus Mill Creek near Saltpetre. Some homes near Kiahsville were impacted. A few homes along Mill Creek were flooded. Small private bridges were washed out. Road culverts were damaged. A couple of vehicles were found in Mill Creek. ||A 62 year old woman tried to walk out of Rowe Hollow in the Amilda vicinity. She was going to attend a Good Friday evening service at the neighborhood church around 1800E on the 3rd. The unnamed run, that flows out of the…

events.title: Debris Flow near Whitcomb
events.description: 1 death. Greenbrier County. A motorist was driving on Coffman Hill Road in the community of Ronceverte, WV when a mudslide spilled across the road, carrying with it a tree. The tree hit the vehicle, causing the fatality of the motorist. The motorist was the only one in the vehicle.

events.title: Heavy Rain near Hemlock
events.description: 5 deaths (indirect). Jackson County. A SUV traveling northbound on Interstate 77 lost control on wet pavement and veered into the median. This occurred at mile marker 143 between Ripley and Ravenswood. The vehicle crashed through a cable median and into the southbound traffic. A pickup truck traveling south hit the broadside of the SUV causing it to catch fire. Five of the 6 people in the SUV were killed. These are considered indirect weather deaths. ||Investigating officers of the WV State Police believed weather played a contributing factor. Areas of moderate rain were in the vicinity.
